title: SIU 'toothless,' says watchdog
article: The civilian agency that investigates police in Ontario was described as "toothless," "timid" and completely ineffective in a scathing report issued Tuesday by the provincial ombudsman.

The Special Investigations Unit "has become so timid and fearful in its watchdog role that police oversight has hit rock bottom in Ontario," said ombudsman Andre Marin as he released Oversight Unseen -- a 121-page report about the effectiveness of the agency.
The SIU motto of "one law" for civilians and police is "empty rhetoric and puffery by an organization that has lost its way," said Marin.
The report points out that of the 226 incidents investigated by the SIU in 2006, charges were laid against officers in two cases.
Windsor lawyer Gino Morga is representing the family of Bryan Dukic, who died after being arrested by Windsor police in April 2006.
Witnesses said that during the arrest he was punched several times in the face and kneed in the torso.
The SIU found the police officers were justified in their use of force and no charges were laid.

"I certainly found in the Dukic case that the SIU was, in fact, toothless in its approach, and I thought could have been much more intense in its investigation," said Morga, who is representing the Dukic family in a lawsuit against Windsor police.
"We learned a lot more things at the inquest (conducted six months ago) that the SIU didn't pick up on."
The coroner's jury classified the death an accident caused by massive internal bleeding from lacerations to the spleen, made worse by liver cirrhosis and trauma to the chest wall.

Windsor police Chief Gary Smith, Windsor Police Association president Ed Parent and Windsor Police Services Board chairman Eddie Francis did not return calls seeking comment on the ombudsman's report.

One local case where the SIU have laid charges against officers involves two Leamington cops, charged with assault for allegedly breaking a man's ribs following a chase in May 2007. They appear in court in November.
There are 45 recommendations to improve the agency in the report, which comes after a more than year-long investigation by the ombudsman.
The recommendations include a call for more transparency by the SIU and the release of the director's reports in each case to the public.

The SIU investigates police when there has been an incident ending in the death or serious bodily harm of a civilian. It is the only agency of its kind in Canada and has been cited as a model by critics in other provinces.
